question_text: Find the length of the chord formed by x² + y² = a² on the line x cos α + y sin α = p.

insider_note: The line is already in normal form, so p IS the perpendicular distance from the origin — recognising that is the whole question, and computing the distance from scratch wastes the time it saves.

steps.label: Read the centre, radius and distance
steps.margin_note: One mark. Say in words that the line is in normal form; that sentence is what earns it.
steps.memory_tip: x cos α + y sin α = p is the normal form, and p is the distance from the origin.

steps.why: In the normal form the coefficients satisfy cos²α + sin²α = 1, so the usual distance formula divides by 1 and the distance is simply p. The centre is the origin, so no further work is needed.
common_mistakes: Computing √(cos²α + sin²α) as something other than 1.
Taking a² as the radius instead of a.

steps.label: Write the length of the chord
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The answer is a formula in a and p; there is nothing numerical to compute.
steps.memory_tip: Length of chord = 2√(r² − p²), with r = a.
steps.why: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, so half the chord is √(r² − p²) by Pythagoras. Here r = a, so the whole chord is 2√(a² − p²). It is real only when p < a, that is when the line actually cuts the circle.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the factor 2 and giving half the chord.
